S54.01.note: The route apps/web/app/chat/customize/page.tsx also opens these three sections. How Settings is opened from the first screen was not traced.
steps: Open Settings from the app.
Find the group headed Customize in the left list.
Click Skills, then Connectors, then Plugins in turn.
Check that all three sit under the one Customize heading, as Expected says.
S54.01.where: Settings > Customize (group heading) > Skills, Connectors, Plugins

steps: Open Settings and click Plugins under Customize.
Look for the Browse and Add buttons above the list.
Check the installed list and the available plugins shown after Browse.
Open Settings and click Skills under Customize.
Click Browse.
Type research-and-citations in the Search skills box.
Check that one skill shows with its name, publisher and description.

S54.04.needs: none to view; an outside account for the service to connect it
steps: Open Settings and click Connectors under Customize.
Look at the list of connectors and the Connect buttons.
Check that each connector shows its status.

S54.05.note: Owner decision is open on this item.
steps: Open Settings, click Plugins under Customize, then click Browse.
Type a plugin name in Search plugins.
Click a plugin, then click Install.
Read the install confirmation, then compare with Expected.

S54.06.needs: an organization admin account in a workspace, and a second member account in the same workspace
S54.06.note: The member-side view was not traced in the code read.
steps: Sign in as an organization admin and open the workspace console.
Under Controls, click Plugins.
Read the publish options Required, Installed by default and Available to install.
Compare with Expected, then check that a member sees the plugin in Settings > Customize > Plugins.

S54.07.needs: a git repository that lists plugins
S54.07.note: The Add menu was read from constants only; its exact layout was not traced.
steps: Open Settings, click Plugins, then click Add.
Click Add marketplace, then Add from a repository.
Type a git repository address in Repository url and click Sync marketplace.
Check that plugins from that repository appear in the list.
S54.07.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > Add > Add marketplace > Add from a repository

S54.08.note: The filter menu label was not found in the constants read.
steps: Open Settings, click Plugins under Customize.
Type Research in Search plugins.
Check that the results narrow to matching plugins.
Use the filter control beside the search box and check the results change.
S54.08.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins, then the Search plugins box

S54.09.note: The plugin detail shows a Category row, but no browse-by-category control was found in DirectoryToolbar.tsx or the directory constants. Searched packages/ui/ui/src/directory and apps/web/features/directory for category controls.

S54.12.note: The More from link shows only when the publisher profile is loaded.
steps: Open a plugin's detail page from Browse.
Find the Publisher row and read the publisher name.
Click the link that reads More from and the publisher name.
Check that the list now shows that publisher's plugins.
S54.12.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > Browse > open a plugin > Publisher

steps: Open Settings, click Plugins, then click Browse.
Type Research in Search plugins.
Click the Research pack card.
Check the detail page shows the name, publisher, version and Includes section.
S54.13.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > Browse > click a plugin

S54.14.needs: none to view; an install is needed for the Use switches
steps: Open a plugin's detail page.
Under Includes, click the Skills tab.
Read the skill names and descriptions.
Install the plugin, then check that each skill has a Use switch.
S54.14.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > Browse > open a plugin > Includes > Skills

S54.15.needs: an outside account for the service
steps: Open a plugin's detail page.
Under Includes, click the Connectors tab.
Read each connector's status: Connected, Not connected or Not added.
Click Connect on one connector and check the status changes.
S54.15.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > Browse > open a plugin > Includes > Connectors

S54.16.note: Agents are usable in the agi CLI, not in the web chat. The CLI command for them was not traced.
steps: Open a plugin's detail page.
Find the Agents row under Includes.
Read the note: Agents run in the agi CLI, not in chat.
Compare with Expected.
S54.16.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > Browse > open a plugin > Includes > Agents

S54.17.note: Where a command is typed to run it was not traced.
steps: Open a plugin's detail page.
Find the Commands row under Includes.
Read the list of commands shown.
S54.17.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > Browse > open a plugin > Includes > Commands

steps: Open a plugin's detail page before installing.
Read the Permissions section and its copy.
Click Install and read the confirmation.
Cancel, then compare with Expected.
S54.19.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > Browse > open a plugin > Permissions

S54.20.note: Owner decision is open on this item.
steps: Open a plugin's detail page.
Find the Works with row and read its chips.
Find the Desktop and CLI text if the plugin is not for this surface.
S54.20.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > Browse > open a plugin > Works with

S54.21.note: The earlier check did not perform an install.
steps: Open a plugin's detail page.
Click Install.
Read the confirmation title that starts with Install.
Confirm and check that the button changes to Uninstall.
S54.21.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > Browse > open a plugin > Install

S54.22.note: There is no button called Configure; settings are the Enabled switch and the per-skill Use switches.
steps: Open an installed plugin's detail page.
Find the Enabled switch and the Use switches for its skills.
Change one Use switch.
Check the change stays after reopening the plugin.
S54.22.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > open an installed plugin

S54.23.needs: an outside account for that service
S54.23.note: The sign-in step was not traced in the code read.
steps: Open an installed plugin's detail page.
Click the Connectors tab under Includes.
Click Connect on a bundled connector.
Complete the sign-in and check the status shows Connected.
S54.23.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > open an installed plugin > Includes > Connectors > Connect

S54.24.note: If the server no longer runs the plugin, the row shows Not available on this surface instead.
steps: Open an installed plugin's detail page.
Turn the Enabled switch off.
Check the plugin is still listed as installed and Uninstall is still there.
Turn Enabled back on.
S54.24.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > open an installed plugin > Enabled

S54.25.needs: an installed plugin that has a newer version
S54.25.note: No separate Update button was found. The version switch is the update path.
steps: Open an installed plugin that has a newer version.
Read the Update available badge and the Installed version row.
Click Choose a version, pick the newer version, then click Switch version.
Read the confirmation, then check the Installed version changed.
S54.25.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > open an installed plugin > Installed version

S54.26.needs: an installed plugin with more than one version
S54.26.note: No control named Pin was found. Choosing a version is the closest match and whether it stops automatic updates was not traced.
steps: Open an installed plugin's detail page.
Find the Installed version row.
Click Choose a version and pick a different version.
Click Switch version, read the confirmation, and check the Installed version row.
S54.26.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > open an installed plugin > Installed version > Choose a version

S54.27.note: The Customize button shows only when the plugin is marked customizable.
steps: Open a plugin's detail page where Customize is shown.
Click Customize and read the confirmation that starts with Customize.
Confirm and open the copy that is made.
Edit one of its skills and check the change is kept.
S54.27.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > open a plugin > Customize

S54.28.note: No visible button says Fork. Customize makes the copy.
steps: Open a plugin's detail page.
Click Customize to make an editable copy.
Check that a copy of the plugin appears with its own skills.
Check the original plugin is unchanged.
S54.28.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > open a plugin > Customize

S54.29.needs: a plugin already installed (install one from Browse first)
S54.29.note: No confirmation dialog is shown for plugin uninstall; the code runs it directly (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/DirectoryPanel.tsx:549). On failure the text is 'Could not uninstall this plugin. Try again.' (apps/web/features/directory/constants.ts:250).
steps: Open Settings, then Customize, then Plugins.
Open a plugin whose header shows Installed.
Click Uninstall in the plugin header.
Look: the plugin should leave the installed list, as Expected says a user can uninstall it.
S54.29.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > open an installed plugin > Uninstall

S54.30.needs: a workspace admin account and a member account in the same workspace; a group if testing the group step
S54.30.note: I found no per-member picker; assignment is by install setting and by group only. The member check in step 5 is my own step, not a labelled screen. Groups must exist first (hint: 'Create a group under Roles', WorkspacePlugins.tsx:232).
steps: Sign in as a workspace admin, open the Workspace section and click Plugins.
Find a plugin the workspace publishes and open its install setting.
Choose Required, Installed by default or Available to install.
For a group setting, pick a group under Choose a group and check the row reads Setting for that group.
Sign in as a member of the same workspace, open Settings > Customize > Plugins, and compare the plugin's state with the setting you chose.

labels.text: Passed. No unsafe patterns were found.
Not scanned. Scans run on plugins you upload or create and on registry versions.

S54.32.needs: none; a plugin with a scan result (check which plugins show a verdict)
S54.32.note: The Security scan section is drawn only when the plugin carries scan data (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/PluginDetailView.tsx:1068).
steps: Open Settings, then Customize, then Plugins.
Open a plugin's detail page.
Scroll below the Permissions section to the Security scan heading.
Compare the verdict text with Expected: Passed, Needs your review, or Blocked, with a Scanned date. If it reads Not scanned, the plugin has no scan yet.
S54.32.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > open a plugin > Security scan

S54.33.needs: an installed plugin the server no longer runs (hard to get on demand); a web account
S54.33.note: The visible warnings I found are about the surface only. I found no version-specific warning text in the cited lines, so the version part of Expected is unconfirmed.
steps: Open Settings, then Customize, then Plugins.
Open a plugin that is not installed. If it reads Desktop and CLI, it is set up from the desktop app or CLI on this surface.
Open an installed plugin the server no longer runs. Look for the warning Not available on this surface.
Read its hint: Still installed, but the server no longer runs it here. Compare with Expected.
S54.33.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > open a plugin

S54.34.needs: an installed plugin whose skill is missing or whose connector is not connected (hard to set up on demand)
S54.34.note: The repair list covers missing skills and missing connectors only. No repair for a missing plugin dependency was found; the dependency wording is only the install message (apps/web/features/directory/constants.ts:348).
steps: Open Settings, then Customize, then Plugins, and open an installed plugin.
Look for a repair row: These skills did not load: with a Reload skills button, or Its skills need the connector with a Connect button.
Click Reload skills or Connect.
Look: the row should clear, or the connector flow should open. Compare with Expected.
S54.34.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > open an installed plugin

S54.35.note: No plugin-creation assistant found. I searched 'assistant' in apps/web/features/directory, packages/ui/ui/src/directory and apps/web/features/plugins. The only creation path is a manual 'Create a plugin' form with Name, Description and Skills fields (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/constants.ts:429). apps/web/lib/services/user-skill-authoring.ts is only an on/off environment guard, not an assistant.

S54.36.needs: a plugin you created or uploaded; a platform admin account for the review step
S54.36.note: The submit button shows when detail.submittable is set (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/DirectoryPanel.tsx:687). I did not check whether an approved submission is then listed.
steps: Open Settings, then Customize, then Plugins, and open a plugin you created or uploaded. The button appears only when the plugin is submittable.
Click Submit to the directory, then Submit for review in the dialog.
Look for the status Submitted for review and a Withdraw button in the plugin detail.
Sign in as a platform admin, open Plugin moderation (/admin/plugins), and filter by Waiting for review to find the submission.
Compare with Expected: the publisher can see the review status.
S54.36.where: Settings > Customize > Plugins > open a plugin you created or uploaded > Submit to the directory

S54.37.needs: a platform admin account; a test plugin version you can safely suspend
S54.37.note: I did not check whether the reason field is required before confirming.
steps: Sign in as a platform admin, open the admin console and click Plugin moderation (/admin/plugins). Other accounts get a not-found page.
Find a plugin and open its versions list.
Click Deprecate or Suspend next to a published version.
Confirm in the dialog (Suspend asks Suspend <name> <version>?).
Look: the version status should change to Deprecated or Suspended. Compare with Expected.
S54.37.where: Admin console > Plugin moderation > open a plugin > Deprecate or Suspend next to a version
